original_value: Aging is associated with a progressive decline in health, resulting in increased medical care and costs. Mobile technology may facilitate health self-management, thus increasing the quality of care and reducing costs. Although the development of technology offers opportunities in monitoring the health of older adults, it is not clear whether these technologies allow older adults to manage their health data themselves. This paper presents a review of the literature on mobile health technologies for older adults, focusing on whether these technologies enable the visualization of monitored data and the self-reporting of additional information by the older adults. The systematic search considered studies published between 2009 and 2019 in five online databases. We screened 609 articles and identified 95 that met our inclusion and exclusion criteria. Smartphones and tablets are the most frequently reported technology for older adults to enter additional data to the one that is monitored automatically. The recorded information is displayed on the monitoring device and screens of external devices such as computers. Future designs of mobile health technology should allow older users to enter additional information and visualize data; this could enable them to understand their own data as well as improve their experience with technology.

result.paraphrase: Aging is linked to a gradual decline in health, which leads to greater medical care needs and higher costs. Mobile technology may support self-management of health, improving care quality and lowering expenses. While technological advances create opportunities to monitor older adults’ health, it remains unclear whether these tools let older adults manage their own health data. This paper reviews the literature on mobile health technologies for older adults, with emphasis on whether they let users visualize monitored data and self-report additional information. The systematic search covered studies published from 2009 to 2019 across five online databases. We screened 609 articles and found 95 that met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Smartphones and tablets are the technology most often reported for older adults to input extra data beyond what is automatically monitored. The recorded information is shown on the monitoring device and on external screens such as computers. Future mobile health technology designs should enable older users to add more information and view data, which may help them understand their own data and enhance their experience with technology.
